The primary task is psychological-health support through reducing help-seekers’ emotional distress; adapted helping-skills procedures, emotional-state measurements and human support experiments make this substantive mental-health-support research, not incidental emotional language.

Primary scientific modeling of human neural/cognitive dynamics. Section 5 explicitly distinguishes its IRF/cognitive questions from engineering performance; Natural Stories fMRI models cortical language-network responses, non-linear BOLD saturation and interactions between structural and string surprisal. This is actual human neural-response research in healthy subjects, not merely NLP evaluated with a brain-data illustration.

Primary experimental question is human sentence-processing mechanism and morphology, tested using reading, eye-tracking and language-network fMRI from 78 subjects. Section 7 fits BOLD responses and interprets differences between latency-based measures and blood oxygenation. The study investigates human neural processing rather than optimizing generic NLP task scores.

Under the clarified co-primary actual-research/experiments criterion, biomedical extraction is a central substantive validation arm, not an incidental benchmark. Beyond PubMed chemical/disease tagging results, Sections 3.4–3.8 center learning dynamics, lexicon-effort comparison, rule-selection ablations, detailed chemical/disease boundary and semantic errors, and an explainability user study on BC5CDR. Domain-general rule induction and CoNLL validation are real counterevidence to sole biomedical scope but do not negate this co-primary biomedical experimental program. No distinct clinical hypothesis or dataset-majority rule is required.

The central novel joint overlapped/discontinuous entity task is experimentally investigated through clinical CLEF notes and CADEC, including clinical entity-specific ablations and detailed comparisons. Section 4 distinguishes supplementary GENIA/ACE05 overlapped-only experiments from the main joint task. Actual clinical extraction research is primary despite a general architecture and an additional news-domain test.

record.reason: INCLUDE as impairment-specific assistive communication research, not merely generic text generation marketed to disabled users: section 5.2 explicitly designs noisy-input robustness for AAC mouth-stick/eye-tracker errors; section 6.1 tests dwell-constrained access based on eye-typing defaults; section 6.2 experimentally uses phrases written by people with ALS for voice banking. Actual patient participants are absent and clinical benefit is not established, but the research design itself is adapted to impairment-specific communication.

Primary impairment-specific AAC objective, not generic generation merely suggested for disabled users. Aphasia lexical/semantic deficits, inability to use orthographic prediction, and difficulty navigating hierarchical vocabularies shape the design: a limited flat set of personally contextualized words, and association-based expansion motivated by aphasia navigation studies. Evaluation operationalizes AAC communication ease versus flexibility as precision/recall over displayed-item counts, using an AAC frequency-vocabulary baseline. This is computational assistive-language support for impairment; no requirement for clinical validation.

Under explicit co-primary criterion, biomedical zero-shot entity recognition is a substantive research arm: adapts MedMentions and UMLS type descriptions, investigates biomedical class confusions (Bacterium, Body Substance, Body System), and compares Metathesaurus/Semantic Network/Wikipedia descriptions with domain-specific interpretation of terminology and ontology limitations (§§4.3–4.4). These dedicated biomedical analyses qualify alongside general-domain experiments; generic architecture alone is not exclusionary.
